proof_summary: Writing $p=2m+1$, Euler’s criterion and a binomial/Vandermonde factorization show that the determinant modulo $p$ vanishes exactly when $(m!)^{m+1}=1$; Wilson’s theorem gives $(m!)^2=(-1)^{m+1}$, making this equivalent to $m$ being odd. Conversely, when $m$ is odd, a quadratic-character sum shows that the product of the original matrix with the transpose of its factorial-sign-reversed analogue is skew-symmetric; the latter matrix has nonzero determinant by the modular criterion, so odd-dimensional skew-symmetry forces the original determinant to vanish.
